threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success metrics, and initial call type mapping for the playbook.

messages.text: Team, welcome to the Omnichannel Customer Service Playbook project! Our goal is to create a unified guide to improve service consistency. First step is T1: mapping our top customer interaction types. Can everyone share the top 3-5 scenarios you see in your areas? This will feed into our initial map, A2.

Great to be on this. For the contact centre, the big ones are: 1. Order status inquiry (Where is my order?), 2. Return/exchange requests, 3. Product availability check (in-store vs online), 4. Payment/billing issues, and 5. Technical support for website/account login.
For in-store sellers we get a lot of 'do you have this in another size/color', questions about product features, and price matching.

In the bookshop, our key interactions are: 1. Specific book search (author/title), 2. Genre/author recommendations ('I liked X, what else would I like?'), 3. Handling special orders for out-of-stock or niche publications, and 4. Questions about author events.
Thanks for kicking this off. Do we have any data on call volumes for the contact centre types? Just to make sure we're prioritizing correctly.
Good question. Yes, I've started populating A2 with the latest volume data from the contact centre reports. @7284's list aligns perfectly with the top 5 by volume.
I've added comments to A2 with the common escalation paths for those top 5. The process for billing issues is particularly inconsistent across teams, so that's a good one to standardize.

Excellent, thanks for that. Combining everyone's input, here is the proposed list of 10 priority interaction types for our playbook. Please review in A2. If there are no objections by EOD, we'll lock this in.
looks good to me
The list in A2 covers the critical scenarios for the bookshop. I approve.
LGTM.

Great, we have consensus. D1 is confirmed: the top 10 interaction types in A2 are our priority. Now, let's talk about success metrics, which is T12. I propose we track: 1. First-Contact Resolution (FCR), 2. Customer Satisfaction (CSAT), and 3. Playbook Adoption Rate by staff. Thoughts?

Those are the right metrics. For FCR, we need to be careful with the definition. Is it 'customer doesn't call back within 48 hours on the same issue'? We should document the exact data source and calculation to be consistent. For CSAT, we can use the post-interaction survey data we already have.
How do we measure adoption rate?

We can track it via the quality monitoring process. One of the scorecard items will be 'adherence to playbook guidelines'. We'll get a percentage from that. @7284, excellent point on FCR. Let's use the 'no repeat contact within 48h' definition. I'll document that.
Can we track sales metrics too? like cross-sells for the in-store team?

Good thought, but let's keep the primary success metrics for this project focused on service quality to avoid muddying the waters. We can track cross-sells as a secondary, channel-specific metric. For now, let's agree on the core three.
Okay, I'm hearing agreement on FCR, CSAT, and Adoption Rate as our primary success metrics. The data sources will be our call log system and post-interaction surveys. I'm marking this as decided.

threads.thread_goal: Draft and iterate on standard call handling and quality monitoring approach.

messages.text: Hi all, I've created the first draft of the standard call scripts (T2) and the quality monitoring scorecard (A3). They are now in the main playbook draft A1. Please take a look and provide your feedback here.

Thanks. I've reviewed the scripts. The opening and closing are solid. For the verification step, I suggest we rephrase 'What is your full name and order number?' to something more conversational like 'To pull up your account, could I please get your full name and order number?'. It's a small change but improves the tone. I've left a few similar suggestions as comments in A1.
The scripts look good. On the scorecard A3, what's the difference between 'Tone' and 'Empathy'?

Good question. 'Tone' is about the vocal delivery (e.g., clear, professional, energetic), while 'Empathy' is about demonstrating understanding of the customer's feelings (e.g., 'I can see how frustrating that must be'). The rubric in A3 has examples for each.
Will these scripts work for in-store too? Some of the language is very call-center specific.

That's a key point. These are the core scripts for the contact centre. We'll be drafting specific in-store versions in the next phase (T4). However, the principles (like the greeting and closing) should be consistent in tone.

On the scorecard A3, I think we should add a specific criterion for 'Correct use of playbook resources'. This will help us measure adoption, as we discussed, and makes it clear that using the new guide is a core expectation. Also, once the scripts are final, I can create a one-page quick-reference sheet for agents as part of T8. That always helps with adoption.
Both are fantastic ideas. I've updated A3 with the new criterion. And yes, please take the lead on T8, a quick-reference checklist (A6) would be invaluable.
I've accepted all your suggested wording changes in A1, @7284. They definitely improve the flow. With those changes, are we ready to approve the v1.0 scripts for the contact centre?
Yes, they look ready for the pilot.
Yes, approved.

Perfect. D3 is confirmed: standard call scripts v1.0 are approved. Now for the scorecard. With the addition of the 'Playbook Adherence' criterion, does anyone have further comments on the criteria or scoring rules in A3?
The scorecard looks comprehensive for call/chat interactions. It covers the key areas well.
The rubric is clear and the examples are helpful. I think it's ready.
Excellent. Then I'm marking this as decided. D4 is confirmed: the quality monitoring scorecard criteria and scoring rules in A3 are approved for the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Define in-store specialised seller and bookshop-specific guidelines.

messages.text: Hi team, I've drafted the first set of sales and cross-sell scripts for specialised sellers (T4). The doc is A5. Let me know what you think.

Thanks for getting this started, @52506. I've had a quick look. The product suggestions are good, but we need to make sure the transition from service to sales feels natural. For example, instead of 'Do you want to buy extended warranty?', maybe something like 'Since you're buying this for travel, some customers also add our travel case to protect it. Can I show you?'. Let's focus on being helpful first.

I agree. It's about solving the customer's stated need first, then anticipating their unstated need. The scripts in A5 could be framed as 'helpful suggestions'. For example: 'Since you've chosen X, you might also find Y useful because...'. This connects the recommendation back to their original purchase.
ok that makes sense. i will rephrase them to be more like suggestions. thanks for the feedback.

Following on from that, I've uploaded my draft for the bookshop recommendation and special order guidelines (T5) to A4. I've focused on a conversational approach to discovering a reader's taste before making a recommendation, and included a clear checklist for handling special publication orders to manage expectations on delivery times.
The guide in A4 is very detailed. Is all of that necessary for every customer? It seems like a lot to remember.

For book lovers, the quality of the recommendation is key to their experience. The guide provides a framework, not a rigid script. It's about asking the right questions to make a thoughtful suggestion. The special order process needs to be precise to avoid errors, hence the detail. We can highlight the key steps in the one-page checklist (A6) that @7284 is creating.
Exactly. The detail in A4 is appropriate for that specialised role. @125944, this is excellent work. I have no changes. I propose we approve the bookshop guidelines as they are.
Thank you. I'm happy with that.
I've updated the scripts in A5 based on the feedback. They should feel more helpful now.
Thanks, @52506. I've reviewed the new versions in A5. The tone is much better now - great improvement. I think these are ready for the pilot. Any final objections to approving these scripts?
The revised scripts are much stronger. I approve.
They look fine.
Okay, that's a consensus. D5 and D6 are confirmed. The core sales/cross-sell scripts and the bookshop guidelines are approved. Great work everyone.

threads.thread_goal: Consolidate the omnichannel playbook and align on shared principles.

messages.text: Team, we're moving on to T7: compiling the full playbook, A1. I've pulled in all the approved content (from A2, A3, A4, A5) and created a table of contents. Please review the structure and let me know if you see any gaps. I also want to align on a set of shared service principles for T6. I've added a draft 'Our Service Principles' section to the intro.
The principles like 'Be helpful' and 'Listen actively' seem good.

The structure of A1 looks logical. I reviewed the principles and suggest adding one more: 'Own the resolution'. This encourages agents and sellers to take responsibility for a customer's issue from start to finish, even if it requires escalation. It's a key part of reducing customer effort.
I strongly support adding 'Own the resolution'. It's critical for complex queries like special orders where follow-up is needed.
That's a great addition, @7284. It perfectly captures the spirit of this project. I've added it to the list in A1. Any other thoughts on the principles?
no, the list is good.
Okay, hearing none, I'm confirming D7: the omnichannel service principles, including 'Own the resolution', are agreed. They will be the first page of the playbook.

Just one small flag on the content. In the in-store returns section, it mentions processing a refund to 'the original card'. In the contact centre section, our script says we can only offer store credit for returns without a receipt. We should align these to avoid confusion if a customer was told something different over the phone.

Excellent catch, @7284. That's exactly the kind of gap we need to close. I've checked with the retail ops manager, and the policy is indeed 'store credit without receipt'. I've updated the in-store section in A1 to match the contact centre process. Thank you for spotting that.
Also, a quick update on T11: the entire playbook content has been reviewed by the legal team, and they've given us the green light. No compliance issues found.
That's great news.
With that final alignment and the legal review complete, are we all comfortable signing off on the content of A1 for the pilot rollout? This will be our v1.0.
Content looks solid. Ready for pilot.
Yes, I sign off.
approved
Fantastic. D8 is confirmed: Playbook v1.0 content is signed off for pilot. I'll finalize the formatting and share the read-only version shortly. Next up: planning the pilot!

threads.thread_goal: Plan pilot training, collect feedback, and define next iteration.

messages.text: Alright team, it's time to pilot our new playbook! As per T9, I've drafted the training plan and schedule in A7. We're looking for one contact centre team and two in-store teams (one general, one bookshop) to participate. Training will be a 2-hour session next week. Please let me know which teams can volunteer.

My team can pilot for the contact centre. We're available for the Tuesday slot listed in A7. Quick question: what's the protocol if an agent in the pilot encounters a situation not covered by the playbook? Should they flag it to their supervisor immediately?
The bookshop team is happy to participate. The Wednesday session works for us. We'll pay close attention to how the recommendation guide flows in real conversations.
I can get my team for the general store pilot. How long is the training?

It's a 2-hour session, all details are in A7. Thanks for volunteering! @7284, great question. Yes, the protocol is to handle the situation with their best judgment, then immediately flag the gap to their supervisor, who will log it in our feedback sheet, A8.
Okay, that's settled then. D9 confirmed: the pilot teams will be @7284's team, @125944's team, and @52506's team. Training dates are confirmed as per A7. I'll send out the calendar invites.

Hi all, jumping forward a week. The pilot is complete! A huge thank you to the participating teams. We've gathered a lot of great feedback in the log (A8) as part of T10. I've synthesized the key themes and want to discuss which improvements to prioritize for v1.1.
My team said the scripts were helpful but they want more examples for different product categories.

The main feedback from my team, which I've detailed in A8, is that the quick-reference checklist was the most used tool. They loved it. The main playbook was seen as a bit dense for in-the-moment use. For v1.1, I suggest we create more checklists for specific complex processes, like the 'billing dispute' workflow.

The bookshop guide was very successful. The team felt more confident in their recommendations. One suggestion for improvement is to add a section on how to gracefully end a conversation when a customer isn't interested in recommendations, to avoid seeming pushy.
Did we see any change in the metrics?

Great question. As part of T12, we looked at the pilot teams' data. It's early, but we saw a 5% increase in FCR for the contact centre team and a small but positive lift in CSAT scores for the in-store teams. A very promising start!

Based on all this fantastic feedback, I propose the following improvements for v1.1: 1. Add more specific examples to the in-store sales scripts. 2. Create a new quick-reference checklist for billing disputes. 3. Add a section to the bookshop guide on gracefully concluding recommendation conversations. Does this list capture the priorities correctly?
Yes, that covers the most critical feedback from my perspective.
Agreed. That addresses our main point.
yes that works

Excellent. D10 is confirmed: we will incorporate those three key improvements into playbook v1.1 before the full rollout. I'll create the tasks for these updates. This has been an incredibly successful pilot. Well done, everyone!
